around.headline: Man attacks woman police officer with iron rod after she asks him to return later
around.summary: A man assaulted a woman police officer with an iron rod in Bengaluru after she asked him to come back later, and police have registered a case, per today's report. It's a reminder that even a routine refusal from an official can escalate fast — if you sense hostility building in any public exchange, step back and call for backup rather than pressing the point.

around.headline: Eid Milad-un-Nabi processions trigger clashes in Basavanagudi and elsewhere in the city
around.summary: Clashes broke out during Eid Milad-un-Nabi processions in parts of Bengaluru including Basavanagudi, leading to six arrests and multiple FIRs for assault and sloganeering, per today's reports. If your route passes near a procession tonight, expect heavier police presence and possible detours — avoid lingering at the edges of any gathering that feels tense.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Hindu, The News Minute

around.headline: BMTC electric bus drivers protest at Jayanagar depot
around.summary: BMTC electric bus drivers staged a protest at the Jayanagar depot today, per today's report. Commuters relying on Jayanagar depot routes should build in extra waiting time or keep a backup option ready this evening.

around.headline: Citizens push back on parks land amendment, human chain planned at Lalbagh
around.summary: Bengaluru residents are opposing a state amendment they say would allow park land to be alienated for other use, with a human chain planned at Lalbagh and local MP Tejasvi Surya urging the governor to return the bill, per today's reports. If you use Lalbagh or a neighbourhood park, this is the civic fight to watch — it could affect whether that green space stays protected.
around.source: The Hindu, The New Indian Express, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Karnataka High Court: a husband cannot compel his wife to do household chores or care for his parents
around.summary: The Karnataka High Court ruled that no man can compel his wife to perform household chores or care for his parents, per today's report. It's a concrete legal precedent worth knowing if you're navigating a matrimonial dispute — such labour can't be treated as an enforceable marital obligation.

around.headline: Nepal flash floods: death toll crosses 350, around 288 Indians still missing
around.summary: Nepal's flash floods have killed more than 350 people, with roughly 288 Indians still reported missing as search operations continue, per today's report. If you have travel plans to Nepal or family or friends there, check current advisories before heading out and watch for updates.

street_smart.title: You're at a Bengaluru club and spot a cockroach scurrying near the food counter, right as today's news breaks about several clubs being pulled up for expired meat and cockroach infestations. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real incident: food safety inspections found expired meat and cockroach infestations at multiple Bengaluru clubs, with Karnataka's health minister stressing kitchen hygiene over dress codes (The News Minute, NDTV, The Times of India). This consumer-safety-at-a-restaurant angle hasn't appeared as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks — recent scenarios covered UPI/cab-fare scams, tanker/road hazards, blackmail, drunk-driving checkpoints, speeding-vehicle reflexes, and two-wheeler parking, not what to do on spotting a hygiene violation at a venue.
street_smart.situation: You've already ordered and started eating. The manager is nearby and clearly wants this handled quietly.

choices.text: Stop eating, photograph the issue along with your bill, and file a complaint with the FSSAI food safety helpline (1800-11-4000) or the FoSCoS portal, in addition to telling the manager.
choices.feedback: Correct. Documentation plus an official channel is what actually triggers an inspection — a verbal complaint to the manager alone is easy to smooth over with an apology and no real fix. The photo and receipt give FSSAI something concrete to act on.

choices.text: Accept the manager's on-the-spot offer of a free meal or refund in exchange for deleting your photos and not mentioning it further.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. The freebie is designed to make your complaint disappear before it reaches anyone who could actually order an inspection — it protects the venue's reputation, not the next diner, and once you delete the evidence you have nothing left to report even if you change your mind later.

choices.text: Post about it immediately on social media without documenting it to any authority.
choices.feedback: This can create public pressure, but it doesn't generate the official record that leads to a health inspection, and a hasty post you can't fully back up could invite a legal notice from the venue.

choices.text: Quietly stop eating and leave without saying anything, planning to just never return.
choices.feedback: This protects only you. It creates no pressure to fix the kitchen and does nothing for the next customer who sits at that counter.

takeaways: The FSSAI food safety complaint helpline is 1800-11-4000, and complaints can also be filed through the FoSCoS portal/app — a photo and your bill both strengthen the report.
A restaurant offering a quiet freebie in exchange for silence is managing the complaint, not fixing the kitchen — insist your complaint is formally logged even if you accept a refund.
Every eatery in Karnataka must display its FSSAI licence number; if a place can't produce one, that alone is worth reporting.
